units.title: Bir anı anlat
units.description: Bir deneyimi ayrıntıları ve duygularıyla anlatmak, 120 kelimelik bir hikâye yazmak
units.guide:
## Bu ünitede yapabileceklerin
- Başından geçen bir olayı ayrıntılarıyla ve duygularınla anlatabilirsin.
- Birinin anısını dinlerken ne olduğunu, ne zaman olduğunu ve nasıl hissettiğini anlayabilirsin.
- Bir blog yazısında olayların sırasını ve yazarın o güne bakışını bulabilirsin.
- Unutamadığın bir günü 120 kelimelik bir hikâye olarak yazabilirsin.

## Strateji
- Anıyı dört parçaya böl: ne zaman ve nerede, ne oldu, ne hissettin, bugün nasıl bakıyorsun.
- Hikâyeyi önce metni görmeden dinle. İlk dinlemede yalnızca "Ne oldu?" sorusuna cevap ara, ikinci dinlemede sayı ve süreleri yakala.
- Gölgelemede (shadow) cümleyi duyar duymaz biraz geriden tekrar et; **I was so nervous that…** gibi duygu cümlelerinin vurgusunu taklit et.
- Olayları **at first, then, at that moment, in the end** ile sırala; dinleyici nerede olduğunu kaybetmesin.
- Duyguyu yalnızca adıyla söyleme, bir ayrıntıyla göster: *My hands were shaking.*

## Model metin
> I'll never forget the day my little brother Kerem graduated from university. At first, I felt nervous. The ceremony was held in a huge hall, and our whole family was there. Then Kerem walked onto the stage. My mother started crying, and I felt incredibly proud. In his speech, he thanked me for my help, and I was so surprised that I couldn't say a word.
>
> But that wasn't the only surprise. Earlier that day, my boss called me and told me that I was the new lead designer. I didn't tell anyone until the ceremony was over, because it was Kerem's big day. In the end, I shared the news, everyone cheered, and my grandmother took us all out for dinner. I've never felt so happy. Looking back now, it was a perfect day for both of us.

İlk paragraf olayı sırayla ve duygularla anlatır (**At first**, **Then**, past simple, **so … that**). İkinci paragraf ikinci sürprizi ekler, **In the end** ile toparlar; **I've never felt so happy** (present perfect) ve **Looking back now** ile bugünkü bakışla biter.

## Türklerin sık hatası
- ❌ I have graduated from university in 2023. ✅ I **graduated** from university in 2023. (Geçmişte belli bir zaman varsa past simple.)
- ❌ The ceremony was held in huge hall. ✅ The ceremony was held in **a** huge hall. (Tekil sayılabilen isimden önce **a/an** unutulmaz.)

exercises.passage:
The night I got lost in İzmir

I've lived in Turkey for four years now, but I still remember my first night here as if it were yesterday. I was twenty-two, I didn't speak a word of Turkish, and my phone had died on the plane.

My hostel was in Karşıyaka, so I took the metro from the airport to the city centre and then a ferry across the bay. It was dark and windy, and I was cold and hungry. When the ferry arrived, I realised that I had no idea where the hostel was. I only had the name of the street, written on a piece of paper.

I asked an old man in a tea garden for help. He didn't speak English, but he looked at my paper, smiled and stood up. Then he walked with me for twenty minutes through narrow streets, and he even carried my suitcase. When we finally found the hostel, he refused to take any money. He just said "Hoş geldin" and walked away.

At that moment I felt embarrassed, relieved and very lucky at the same time. I never found out his name, so I've never been able to thank him properly.

That night taught me something important. Now, when I see a tourist with a map and a worried face, I always stop and ask if they need help. It's the least I can do.

nodes.description: Kerem ilk iş gününü görüntülü aramada Sam'e anlatıyor

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: Kerem! Elif told me you started your first job this week. How did it go?
steps.translation: Kerem! Elif bu hafta ilk işine başladığını söyledi. Nasıl geçti?

steps.speaker: Kerem
steps.text: Honestly, Sam, my first day was a disaster, but now I can laugh about it.
steps.translation: Açıkçası Sam, ilk günüm tam bir felaketti ama artık gülüp geçebiliyorum.

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Tell him the whole story. It's even funnier the second time.
steps.translation: Ona her şeyi anlat. İkinci kez dinleyince daha da komik.

steps.speaker: Kerem
steps.text: Well, I was so nervous that I woke up at five and couldn't get back to sleep.
steps.translation: Şöyle ki, o kadar gergindim ki saat beşte uyandım ve bir daha uyuyamadım.

steps.speaker: Kerem
steps.text: I left home really early, but the metro broke down between two stations.
steps.translation: Evden çok erken çıktım ama metro iki istasyonun arasında bozuldu.

steps.speaker: Kerem
steps.text: We were stuck in a dark tunnel for forty minutes, and nobody could use their phones.
steps.translation: Karanlık bir tünelde kırk dakika mahsur kaldık ve kimse telefonunu kullanamadı.

steps.speaker: Kerem
steps.text: There was a woman next to me who looked really worried, so I gave her my bottle of water.
steps.translation: Yanımda çok endişeli görünen bir kadın vardı, ben de ona su şişemi verdim.

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: Oh no! So you were late on your very first day?
steps.translation: Eyvah! Yani daha ilk gününde geç mi kaldın?

steps.speaker: Kerem
steps.text: Only ten minutes, but I ran from the station, so I arrived hot and out of breath.
steps.translation: Sadece on dakika ama istasyondan koştum, bu yüzden terli ve nefes nefese vardım.

steps.speaker: Kerem
steps.text: Then the receptionist told me that the manager was waiting for me in the meeting room.
steps.translation: Sonra resepsiyonist yöneticinin beni toplantı odasında beklediğini söyledi.

steps.speaker: Kerem
steps.text: I walked in, and I recognised her immediately. She was the woman from the metro!
steps.translation: İçeri girdim ve onu hemen tanıdım. Metrodaki kadındı!

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: That's brilliant! What did she say?
steps.translation: Harika! Ne dedi?

steps.speaker: Kerem
steps.text: She laughed and said that I'd already passed my first test: helping a colleague.
steps.translation: Güldü ve ilk sınavımı çoktan geçtiğimi söyledi: bir iş arkadaşına yardım etmek.

steps.prompt: "She laughed and said that I'd already passed my first test" cümlesindeki "She" kimi anlatıyor?

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: So how did you feel at the end of the day?
steps.translation: Peki günün sonunda nasıl hissettin?

steps.speaker: Kerem

steps.translation: Bitkin ama çok gururlu. Beş gündür orada çalışıyorum ve bayılıyorum.

steps.prompt: Kerem ne zamandır yeni işinde çalışıyor?

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: And he's been leaving home an hour early every morning since then!
steps.translation: Ve o günden beri her sabah evden bir saat erken çıkıyor!

steps.speaker: Kerem
steps.text: Of course. I'm never going to be late again, not even for a minute.
steps.translation: Tabii ki. Bir daha asla geç kalmayacağım, bir dakika bile.

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: Good plan. And next time, take two bottles of water, just in case.
steps.translation: İyi plan. Bir dahaki sefere de ne olur ne olmaz iki şişe su al.

units.title: Haberi aktar
units.description: Kısa bir haberin ana noktalarını anlamak ve başkasına aktarmak
units.guide:
## Bu ünitede yapabileceklerin
- Kısa bir radyo haberinden ana bilgiyi ve önemli ayrıntıları anlayabilirsin.
- Bir haberin ana noktalarını başka birine kısaca aktarabilirsin (**aracılık**).
- İngilizce bir haber yazısında ana fikri, ayrıntıları ve yazarın tutumunu bulabilirsin.
- Türkçe bir haberi ya da notu, Türkçe bilmeyen bir arkadaşın için İngilizce özetleyebilirsin.

## Strateji
- Haberi önce metni görmeden dinle ve kendine sor: **Ne oldu? Nerede? Kimi etkiliyor? Ne yapmak gerekiyor?**
- Özetlerken her şeyi çevirme. Karşındaki kişi için önemli olan 3 noktayı seç, gerisini bırak.
- Kaynağı söyle: **According to the radio…, They said that…, The news says…**
- Haberlerde edilgen yapı çok kullanılır: *was cancelled, will be held, has been delayed*. Gölgelemede bu kalıpları ritmiyle tekrar et.
- Aktarırken zamanı kaydır: *"The ferries are cancelled."* → *They said the ferries were cancelled.*

## Model metin
> Hi Sam,
>
> Good news! I've just read about the olive harvest festival in Ayvalık. This year it will be held from 20 to 22 October. During the festival, visitors can take part in the olive picking in the villages for free, so you could try it with Dede! There will also be a concert at the harbour on Saturday evening. However, if it rains, the concert will be moved to the culture centre. Shall I book us a room in a small hotel?
>
> Elif

Mesaj selamla başlar, ilk cümle konuyu verir. Sonra haberin üç ana noktası (tarih, ücretsiz etkinlik, konser ve yağmur durumu) **also** ve **however** ile sıralanır. Son soru Sam'i harekete geçirir.

## Türklerin sık hatası
- ❌ The festival will held in October. ✅ The festival will **be held** in October. (Gelecekteki edilgen: **will be + V3**.)
- ❌ The concert will be moved at the culture centre. / in 20 October ✅ moved **to** the culture centre / **on** 20 October (yön için **to**, tarih için **on**).

İZMİR – Ferry passengers in İzmir can now see exactly when their boat will arrive, thanks to a new free app called İskele. The app was launched on Monday, and it has already been downloaded more than 40,000 times.

The app was designed by Martı Apps, a small technology company in the city. It shows a live map of every ferry in the bay, and it sends a message to passengers if a boat is late or cancelled. Users can also see how crowded each ferry is before they get on.

"We used to wait at the pier without any information," said Ayşe Demir, a teacher who takes the ferry from Karşıyaka every day. "Now I check the app before I leave home, and I haven't missed a boat since Monday."

Elif Erdem, the company's lead designer, said that the team had tested the app with hundreds of passengers. "Older passengers asked us to make the buttons bigger, so we did," she explained.

Not everyone is happy, however. Some passengers have complained that the app doesn't work well at metro stations near the piers. The company says this problem will be fixed in the next update.

The city council hopes the app will persuade more people to leave their cars at home. "If more people took the ferry, the roads would be much less crowded," a spokesperson said.

units.description: Bir şirkete ya da belediyeye resmî bir şikâyet veya talep yazmak
units.guide:
## Bu ünitede yapabileceklerin
- Bir şirkete ya da belediyeye resmî bir şikâyet veya talep e-postası yazabilirsin.
- Telefonda bir sorunu kibarca ama net anlatıp çözüm isteyebilirsin.
- Resmî bir şikâyet e-postasında sorunu, yazarın isteğini ve tutumunu bulabilirsin.
- Müşteri hizmetleri konuşmasından tarih, saat ve verilen sözleri anlayabilirsin.

## Strateji
- E-postayı paragraflara böl: neden yazıyorsun, ne oldu (tarih ve ayrıntılar), ne istiyorsun.
- Size söyleneni aktar: **I was told that…, An agent promised that…** Bu, şikâyetini güçlendirir.
- Kızgın olsan da kibar kalıplar kullan: **I would be grateful if you could…, Could you please…?**
- Hikâyeyi önce metni görmeden dinle; görevlinin verdiği saat ve sözleri not et, sonra soruları cevapla.
- Gölgelemede **I'm afraid…** ve **Would you mind…?** gibi kalıpların düşen tonunu taklit et: kibarlık seste de duyulur.

## Model metin
> Subject: Complaint about our office move on 3 March
>
> Dear Sir or Madam,
>
> I am writing to complain about the service we received from your company during our office move on 3 March.
>
> First, your team arrived three hours late, so we lost most of the working day. When I called your office, I was told that the van was stuck in traffic, but nobody contacted us before that.
>
> Second, two of our computer screens were damaged during the move. They were packed carefully by our staff, so we believe they were broken in your van. I have attached photos of the damaged screens and a copy of the invoice.
>
> I would be grateful if you could pay for the repairs. Could you please reply by the end of next week?
>
> Yours faithfully,
> Elif Erdem
> Lead Designer, Martı Apps

Konu satırı sorunu özetler. İlk paragraf yazma nedenini verir; **First** ve **Second** ile iki sorun ayrı paragraflarda anlatılır (edilgen ve aktarılan söz). Son paragraf kibar bir istek ve son tarih içerir; **Dear Sir or Madam** ile başlayan e-posta **Yours faithfully** ile biter.

## Türklerin sık hatası
- ❌ I have called you last Friday. ✅ I **called** you last Friday. / I **have called** you four times. (Belli bir geçmiş zaman → past simple; zaman belirtmeden toplam deneyim → present perfect.)
- ❌ I am writing to complain for the service. ✅ I am writing to complain **about the** service. (Fiille birlikte gelen edat ve belirli artikel.)

## Beceri testi
Bölüm 5 beceri testi 20 sorudur; geçmek için %80 doğru yap. Bölüm 5, bu test **ve** bu ünitenin yazma görevi (l4, resmî şikâyet e-postası) bitince **tamamlandı** sayılır.

| Bölüm | Soru | Ölçtüğü hedef |
|---|---|---|
| Dinleme | 6 | Anı ve duygular (s5u13, s5u12); haber (s5u14); resmî talep (s5u15); used to (s5u3); aktarılan söz (s5u7) |
| Okuma | 8 | Bir anı yazısında olaylar, çıkarım ve tutum (s5u13); bir haberin ana noktaları (s5u14) |
| Yazma | 4 | Ne zamandır (s5u1–s5u2); haberi aktarma ve edilgen (s5u14, s5u4); şikâyet (s5u15); tahmin (s5u9) |
| Dil | 2 | used to (s5u3); reported speech (s5u7) |

Subject: Lost suitcase – flight from London, 14 March

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to complain about the way my case has been handled since my flight from London to İzmir on 14 March.

When I arrived in İzmir, my suitcase was not on the belt. I reported the problem at your desk in the airport immediately, and I was told that the suitcase would be delivered to my hotel within two days.

However, it has now been eleven days, and I still have not received it. I have called your customer service line four times. Each time I was asked to wait, and twice the call was cut off. Last Friday, an agent promised that someone would call me back the same day, but nobody did.

The suitcase contains the charger for my work laptop and several gifts for friends, so this situation has caused me serious problems. I have had to buy a new charger and some clothes, and I have kept all the receipts.

I would be grateful if you could find my suitcase and deliver it as soon as possible. I would also like you to pay for the items I have had to buy. I have attached copies of my receipts and my boarding pass.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully,
Sam Baker

steps.speaker: Selin
steps.text: Welcome to our new office, everyone! Isn't the sea view wonderful?
steps.translation: Yeni ofisimize hoş geldiniz! Deniz manzarası harika değil mi?

steps.speaker: Mia
steps.text: It's beautiful. I can even see the ferries from my desk!
steps.translation: Çok güzel. Masamdan vapurları bile görebiliyorum!

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: The view is great, Selin, but there's one small problem. The internet isn't working.
steps.translation: Manzara güzel Selin ama küçük bir sorun var. İnternet çalışmıyor.

steps.speaker: Mia
steps.text: It can't be the cables. The technician checked them yesterday.
steps.translation: Kablolar olamaz. Teknisyen dün onları kontrol etti.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Then it must be the internet company. They promised to connect us before Monday.
steps.translation: O zaman internet şirketi olmalı. Bizi pazartesiden önce bağlayacaklarına söz vermişlerdi.

steps.speaker: Selin
steps.text: Elif, could you call them? You're the calmest person in this office.
steps.translation: Elif, onları arayabilir misin? Bu ofisteki en sakin kişi sensin.

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Hello, I'm calling from Martı Apps. Our new office still hasn't been connected.
steps.translation: Merhaba, Martı Apps'ten arıyorum. Yeni ofisimiz hâlâ bağlanmadı.

steps.speaker: Görevli
steps.text: I'm sorry to hear that. Could you give me your customer number, please?
steps.translation: Bunu duyduğuma üzüldüm. Müşteri numaranızı verebilir misiniz lütfen?

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Of course. We were told that everything would be ready by last Friday.
steps.translation: Tabii. Bize her şeyin geçen cumaya kadar hazır olacağı söylenmişti.

steps.speaker: Görevli
steps.text: Let me check. I'm afraid the connection was planned for next Friday, not last Friday.
steps.translation: Kontrol edeyim. Korkarım bağlantı geçen cuma değil, gelecek cuma için planlanmış.

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Next Friday? We can't wait a whole week. Six people can't do their jobs without the internet.
steps.translation: Gelecek cuma mı? Koca bir hafta bekleyemeyiz. Altı kişi internetsiz işini yapamaz.

steps.speaker: Görevli
steps.text: I understand. I can send a technician tomorrow morning, between nine and twelve.
steps.translation: Anlıyorum. Yarın sabah dokuzla on iki arasında bir teknisyen gönderebilirim.

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Thank you. Could you also send me an email to confirm that, please?
steps.translation: Teşekkürler. Bunu onaylayan bir e-posta da gönderebilir misiniz lütfen?

steps.speaker: Görevli
steps.text: Of course. And as an apology, your first month will be free.
steps.translation: Elbette. Ayrıca özür olarak ilk ayınız ücretsiz olacak.

steps.prompt: Şirket özür olarak ne teklif etti?

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Good news, everyone. A technician is coming tomorrow, and they said the first month would be free.
steps.translation: Herkese iyi haber. Yarın bir teknisyen geliyor ve ilk ayın ücretsiz olacağını söylediler.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: A free month! Elif, you should make all our phone calls from now on.
steps.translation: Bir ay bedava! Elif, bundan sonra bütün telefonlarımızı sen yapmalısın.

steps.speaker: Mia
steps.text: So what do we do today without the internet?
steps.translation: Peki bugün internetsiz ne yapacağız?

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Kerem said his office had the same problem last month. They worked from a café for two days.
steps.translation: Kerem geçen ay kendi ofislerinde de aynı sorunun olduğunu söyledi. İki gün bir kafeden çalışmışlar.

steps.speaker: Selin
steps.text: We could have our first meeting on the balcony. It's too nice to stay inside.
steps.translation: İlk toplantımızı balkonda yapabiliriz. İçeride kalmak için hava fazla güzel.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: A meeting with a sea view and no emails? This is the best office ever.
steps.translation: Deniz manzaralı ve e-postasız bir toplantı mı? Bu gelmiş geçmiş en iyi ofis.

Subject: Complaint about our office move on 3 March

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to complain about the service we received from your company during our office move on 3 March.

First, your team arrived three hours late, so we lost most of the working day. When I called your office, I was told that the van was stuck in traffic, but nobody contacted us before that.

I would be grateful if you could pay for the repairs. Could you please reply by the end of next week?

Yours faithfully,
Elif Erdem

Three days in the olive groves
by Sam

Last October, I spent three days in Ayvalık with my friend Elif and her grandparents. I went for the olive harvest festival, but I came home with much more than photos.

On the first morning, Elif's grandfather woke us up at six. I was tired and a bit grumpy, but when we arrived at the grove, the view of the sea made me forget about sleep. We spread nets under the trees and shook the branches for hours. By lunchtime, my arms were aching, and I was covered in leaves.

On Saturday evening, the concert was moved to the culture centre because of the rain, but we were too tired to go. So we stayed at home and listened to Dede's stories instead. He used to work in the same groves when he was a boy, and he still knows every tree.

Honestly, I didn't expect a festival to be so tiring. But it's one of the best trips I've ever had, and I've already booked my flight for next year.

İZMİR – Children in İzmir will soon be able to learn app design for free. Martı Apps, the local company behind the popular ferry app İskele, has announced that it will open free design workshops for children aged 10 to 14.

The workshops will be held every Saturday morning at the company's new office by the sea, starting in May. Each group will have twelve children, and laptops will be provided by the company.

The idea came from Elif Erdem, the company's lead designer, who said that she had always dreamed of a design school for children. "When I was young, I used to draw apps on paper because we didn't have a computer at home," she explained.

Places are limited, and parents can apply on the company's website until 20 April. Several local schools have already shown interest, so the company expects the first groups to fill up quickly.
